label: canon4-je-n3
_why: canon-4rung (§10.69) with ONE change: the research-event parameters restored to the six-rung canon's level on the four-rung anchors — thresholds_by_era 30k/30k/120k/480k → 5k/15k/45k/135k (rule-D keys 4/5 → 135k/405k), industry bar 72 → 36 months, war bar 12 → 6 (config/mod_config.canon4-je.json; field diff against the canon: the research_events block only). User's hypothesis (2026-09-03): 'when we bring them back to the old level (or slightly lower), this gets balanced to better equilibria'. Measured cause (F101): the four-rung book fires ~620–690 JE completions per run over ~150 countries (GBR 15–25, USA 3–9, FRA 0–3; 13–20 of 40 covered technologies) against the six-rung canon's ~4,700–4,800 over ~335 countries (GBR 79–86, USA 80–82, FRA 8–34), and its technology pace is exactly vanilla's (GBR 163 techs at 1935 = vanilla's 163; the six-rung canon 196) — make_tier4_config had re-derived the thresholds ×4 per rung from a 30k base and halved the tick. n=3; 1836 → 1936.1.1; compared against canon-4rung (20260903_000418 growth seeds + 20260903_094941, the same book) and vanilla n=16.

_arms.canon4-je: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.canon4-je.json} — canon-4rung + the six-rung research-event parameters; sha DC42F819…

_delta: vs canon-4rung: the research_events block only (thresholds, bar lengths); recipes, costs, ai_value, techs, companies identical. The emitted journal entries are the same 120 (40 technologies) — their bars fill 2× faster and their sources qualify at 2–6× fewer employees.

_predictions.P1_firings: JE completions per run ≥ 2,000 (canon-4rung 620–690), GBR ≥ 50, USA ≥ 40, FRA ≥ 5; techs with ≥1 completion ≥ 30 of 40.
_predictions.P2_pace: Technology pace ahead of vanilla: GBR technologies held at 1900 ≥ 135 (canon-4rung 128 = vanilla 125) and at 1935 ≥ 175 (163).
_predictions.P3_frontier: Earlier frontier rungs: British plastics glassworks and rubber-grip tooling levels at 1905 above the canon's (10–12 / 9–56); shortlist e0 headcount at 1935 below the canon's 695–850k; the e1 rung no longer the largest at 1935 in at least one seed.
_predictions.P4_gdp: World GDP 0.90–1.05× vanilla (the six-rung canon's JEs raised GDP; the four-rung book's capacity pricing may absorb it).
_predictions.P6_stall: Stall count reported (family 1 in 7); a stall is an outcome, not a defect.
_predictions.P7_risk: If P1 passes and P3 fails, faster technology does not by itself move the ladder — the price/wage death mechanism still gates it (F97).

_watch: first run: JE completion count from debug.log (PMR_JE), GBR/FRA/USA technologies held at 1900 vs the canon, first_run_decomp, company_check
_cost: 3 × 1836→1936, ~2.6 h each: ~8 h. NOT LAUNCHED — awaiting the user's go.
_caveats: n=3 against n=4 on the same book: the JE-count and tech-pace predictions resolve; GDP under ~10% does not.

The four-rung tree covers 40 technologies with JEs against the six-rung canon's 201 today (378 at the time of its runs), so 'back to the old level' restores the per-JE parameters, not the number of JEs.
